question.text: Three concentric spherical metallic shells <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>Y</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi></math> of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi></math> respectively <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo><</mo><mi>b</mi><mo><</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> have surface charge densities <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>σ</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>–</mo><mo> </mo><mi>σ</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>σ</mi></math>, respectively. The shells <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi></math> are at same potential. If the radii of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi><mo> </mo><mo>&</mo><mo> </mo><mi>Y</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>, respectively. The radius of shell <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi></math> is _____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>.

solution.text:
The charges on the spheres are

 qX=σ4πa2qY=-σ4πb2qZ=σ4πc2 

It is given that VX=VZ

So, 

qX4πε0a+qY4πε0b+qZ4πε0c=qX4πε0c+qY4πε0c+qZ4πε0c⇒σ4πa2a-σ4πb2b+σ4πc2c=σ4π(a2-b2+c2)c⇒c(a-b+c)=(a2-b2+c2)⇒c=a+b=2 cm+3 cm=5 cm
